note: Study skeleton paraphrased from the course scope (not verbatim College Board prose; unit numbers are our own sequencing, not official CED numbers). Skill codes are indicative: 1.x concept, 2.x/3.x skill.

objectives.statement: Explain how primitive types, variables, and objects store and represent data in Java.
Write expressions using casting, operators, and String methods to manipulate data.
Explain how Boolean expressions control program flow.
Write if/else chains and nested conditionals to implement decisions.
Write while and for loops, including nested loops, to repeat processes.
Explain encapsulation and how constructors and methods define object behavior.
Design classes with instance variables, constructors, accessors, and mutators.
Apply inheritance, polymorphism, and interfaces to extend and override behavior.
Explain how arrays and ArrayLists store ordered collections and how they differ.
Traverse, insert into, and remove from arrays and ArrayLists without index errors.
Explain row-major traversal of two-dimensional arrays.
Write nested-loop algorithms that process rows, columns, and diagonals of 2D arrays.
Explain base cases and recursive calls and how the call stack unwinds.
Write recursive methods for problems like factorial, string processing, and traversals.
Explain the efficiency trade-offs of sequential versus binary search.
Implement binary search on sorted data.
Implement selection, insertion, and merge sorts and compare their performance.
